extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys/agents facing USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings, and counsel/adjudicators handling such matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules the USPTO uses to decide whether to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state bar's disciplinary adjudication, including the Selling v. Radford exceptions and related due-process/infirmity/grave-injustice analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO reciprocal-discipline standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates, and the USPTO Director finds there is a genuine issue of material fact that: (i) The procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process; (ii) There was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject; (iii) The imposition of the same public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension or disciplinary disqualification by the Office would result in a grave injustice; or (iv) Any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation mirrors the Selling standard; a practitioner seeking to avoid identical federal discipline must identify a genuine issue of material fact as to one of these enumerated bases and must do so by clear and convincing evidence. Absent such a showing, identical discipline is imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling v. Radford presumption and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: State disbarment (or state disciplinary action) creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper unless an independent review reveals: (1) a want of due process; (2) an infirmity of proof of the misconduct; or (3) that grave injustice would result from imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts and the USPTO apply Selling; the practitioner bears the burden of proof to overcome the presumption. The standard is narrow — the USPTO is not a court of review to discover errors in the state adjudication except insofar as one of the Selling exceptions is clearly and convincingly shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner's burden: clear-and-convincing evidence of genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In reciprocal discipline cases, it is the respondent attorney's burden to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling elements precludes reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a high evidentiary burden; mere disagreement or relitigation of substantive issues in the state proceeding is insufficient. The practitioner must produce evidence creating a genuine issue of material fact as to due process, infirmity of proof, or grave injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due-process requirements in disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental requirement of due process is the opportunity to be heard at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner. In disciplinary proceedings, due process includes reasonable notice of the charges, representation by counsel, an opportunity to present evidence, to testify, to cross-examine witnesses, and to present argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show deprivation of due process for purposes of blocking reciprocal discipline, a practitioner must show procedures were so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation. Merely disagreeing with findings or rearguing substantive issues does not meet this test. Participation in hearings with counsel and opportunity to call/cross-examine witnesses ordinarily satisfies due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infirmity of proof standard
rubrics_metrics.description: There must have been such an infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The infirmity-of-proof exception requires showing that the state proceeding's proof was so deficient that the USPTO could not accept the result. This is a narrow standard and requires convincing evidence of serious evidentiary failings, not merely disagreements about credibility or weight of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave-injustice standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The imposition of the same public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension or disciplinary disqualification by the Office would result in a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This looks at whether the severity of the punishment 'fits' the misconduct. If the state discipline was within the range of appropriate sanctions, reciprocal discipline is not a grave injustice. Voluntary stipulations/agreements to sanctions by the practitioner weigh heavily against a grave-injustice claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABA Standards factors for imposing lawyer sanctions (as used in state sanction analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions analysis (per the ABA Standards) considers four factors: (1) the ethical duty violated; (2) the attorney's mental state; (3) the actual or potential injury; and (4) the existence of aggravating and mitigating circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State disciplinary bodies (and stipulations) frequently rely on ABA Standards §§ referenced (e.g., §§ 6.2, 7.2, 9, 9.2, 9.3, 9.22, 9.32). These factors show how a state arrived at a sanction and inform whether that sanction is within an appropriate range for reciprocal-discipline analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timeline and notice requirement for Responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When the OED Director files a Request/Complaint under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the USPTO issues a Notice and Order providing the practitioner an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of a Response is required to raise Selling-type defenses; the USPTO Director will consider any timely-filed response and the OED Director may be ordered to reply. Failure to file a reply to OED's response (if permitted) may forfeit further argument but does not relieve the practitioner's burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to impose identical discipline absent successful challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office 'shall impose the identical' sanction (public censure, reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification) unless the practitioner meets the § 11.24(d) showing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a strong default of reciprocity; the USPTO does not modify the sanction unless one of the narrow exceptions is proved. The Director's role is not to reweigh or re-adjudicate the state proceeding absent clear and convincing evidence of a Selling-type defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of voluntary stipulation/consent to sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's voluntary stipulation to facts and to the sanction in the state proceeding (including drafting and signing the stipulation with counsel) undermines claims of due process deprivation or grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts and the USPTO treat voluntary agreements resolving state discipline as strong evidence that the sanction was freely and properly imposed; this history makes it difficult for the practitioner to show Selling exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and inter-agency notice obligations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.59, 11.58 and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following imposition of discipline, the OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the sample and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public; the practitioner shall comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-discipline administrative steps include publication and notice to other jurisdictions and courts. The Official Gazette notice is to be materially consistent with the provided template; practitioners must also follow registration/notification duties under § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relitigation of substantive state-adjudication matters is not a basis for blocking reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's attempt to relitigate substantive issues or reargue the merits of the underlying state disciplinary matter is not equivalent to showing a due process deprivation or other Selling exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments rehashing the underlying litigation or alleging substantive injustices in the original case (e.g., misconduct of opposing counsel, judicial complaints, or unfavorable civil-case outcomes) do not ordinarily create a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d). The focus is on procedural sufficiency and evidentiary integrity, not reexamination of merits.
